source_text: Deus loquitur ad homines in Scripturis. Aliqui Deum corporeum fingunt; philosophi fabulosa rident. Nos Deum incorporeum invisibilem confitemur, et tamen curare mortalia, nihil sine providentia geri.
pass_a_gloss: God speaks to humans in Scriptures. Some God bodily invent; philosophers fabulous things mock. We God bodiless invisible confess, and yet to-care-for mortal-things, nothing without providence to-be-done.
pass_b_english: God speaks to humans in the Scriptures. Some invent a bodily God; philosophers mock it as fable. We confess God [[bodiless and invisible >> Bible:1 Timothy 1:17]], and yet that he cares for mortal things, and that [[nothing is done apart from his providence >> Bible:Matthew 10:29]].
